Description: Review Priority Model routes some groups of applicants to Enhanced Review or Recommend Decline more often than comparable applicants
Cause: Trained on past adjudicator decisions; features such as FSA and employer may act as proxies for protected characteristics; no direct demographic data to test with; thin-file and newcomer applicants underrepresented
Potential Impact: Denial of credit to eligible applicants; human rights complaints; supervisory scrutiny; reputational harm
Affected Stakeholders: Applicants (newcomers; Indigenous; racialized; older; rural and lower-income); Northstar; regulators
Existing Controls: Enterprise model risk policy; existing credit decision review and complaints process; design intent to exclude age; name; language and marital status from model features
Control Gap: Feature exclusion not verified (OI-03); no agreed fairness metrics or thresholds (OI-07); no approved proxy-testing method; lawfulness of inferring protected attributes unconfirmed (OI-09)
Recommended Control: Verify feature exclusion and audit FSA and employer as proxies before build freeze; run pre-deployment fairness testing using geographic and name-based analysis plus synthetic matched pairs; monitor monthly after launch against committee-approved thresholds
KRI/KPI: Ratio of Enhanced Review and Recommend Decline rates between proxy-inferred groups and a reference group (0.80 screening ratio proposed; not a Canadian legal standard); matched-pair outcome gap
Escalation Trigger: Ratio below 0.80 in any month or below 0.90 for two consecutive months: notify AI Governance Committee within 5 business days and pause any rollout expansion
ISO 42001 Mapping: Cl. 6.1.4 and 8.4 (AI system impact assessment); Annex A.7 (data for AI systems)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 10(2) (bias examination and mitigation); Art. 9; Annex III point 5(b) (creditworthiness). Benchmark only
Intake Reference: Sections F; J; K; OI-03; OI-07; OI-09

Description: Score or recommended path is wrong so risky files receive Standard Review or sound files receive Recommend Decline
Cause: Labels reflect past decisions; declined applicants have no repayment outcome (reject inference); six-year training window may not match current conditions; outcomes lag 6 to 12 months so errors surface late
Potential Impact: Credit losses; wrongful declines; inconsistent review depth; loss of adjudicator trust
Existing Controls: Enterprise model risk policy requires independent validation; adjudicators review every file
Control Gap: Beacon validation not yet performed; reject inference approach not documented; no agreed performance tolerances; no backtesting plan
Recommended Control: Independent validation by Model Risk Management before pilot including out-of-time and segment testing; documented reject inference approach; agreed performance tolerances; quarterly backtesting as outcomes mature
KRI/KPI: Gini (rank-ordering) versus validation baseline; loss rate of Standard Review path versus Enhanced Review path; performance by segment
Escalation Trigger: Gini falls more than 10 percent relative to baseline or a segment gap exceeds tolerance: notify Model Risk Management within 5 business days
ISO 42001 Mapping: Cl. 8.2; Annex A.6 (AI system life cycle)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 15 (accuracy and robustness); Art. 9. Benchmark only

AI Risk: Automation bias and anchoring on the recommendation
Description: Adjudicators follow the recommended path without forming an independent view so Recommend Decline becomes the de facto decision
Cause: Time pressure (Beacon targets 20 percent faster handling); recommendation is visible before the adjudicator forms a view; scores appear authoritative; no training on model limitations
Potential Impact: Wrongful declines at scale; loss of the human review that keeps Beacon assistive; tier rises to Critical if concordance exceeds 90 percent
Existing Controls: Adjudicators hold delegated lending authority and can override any recommendation
Control Gap: No rationale requirement; override tracking not built (OI-06); no training on model limits or automation bias; no concordance baseline
Recommended Control: Written rationale required when following Recommend Decline; blind re-review of a random sample where the adjudicator decides before seeing the recommendation; concordance and override monitoring by adjudicator and team; training before pilot
KRI/KPI: Concordance rate with Recommend Decline; override rate; median review time on Recommend Decline files versus baseline
Escalation Trigger: Team concordance above 90 percent over a month or override rate below 3 percent: AI Governance Office review and tier reassessment (see methodology sensitivity table)
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.9 (use of AI systems); Cl. 7.2 (competence)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 14(4)(b) (awareness of automation bias); Art. 26 (deployer oversight). Benchmark only

AI Risk: Human oversight exists in name only
Description: Adjudicators lack the time; skills; authority or evidence trail to challenge Beacon so oversight cannot be demonstrated to auditors or supervisors
Cause: Override and rationale capture not built; training covers credit judgment but not model limits; review time shrinks after rollout; no defined rule for when override or escalation is mandatory
Potential Impact: Failure of the primary safeguard; inability to evidence oversight; adverse audit or supervisory findings
Existing Controls: Delegated lending authority; logging of inputs; scores and adjudicator actions is designed into the Workbench
Control Gap: Override and rationale capture not built (OI-06); mandatory override and escalation rules undefined; no capacity monitoring; no fallback if logging fails
Recommended Control: Build override and rationale capture before pilot; define mandatory override and escalation triggers in the Human Oversight Framework; monitor time per file and queue pressure; suspend the Recommend Decline display if logging is down for more than 24 hours
KRI/KPI: Percent of files with follow or override rationale captured (target 100 percent for Recommend Decline); median review time per file versus baseline; percent of adjudicators trained
Escalation Trigger: Capture rate below 98 percent in a week or logging outage above 24 hours: suspend Recommend Decline display and notify AI Governance Office
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.9; Annex A.6 (operation and monitoring); Cl. 9.1

Description: Applicants or adjudicators cannot get a meaningful reason for a recommendation; LLM summaries may state things the source documents do not support
Cause: Reason codes not validated as faithful to the model; LLM summaries are not explainable; adverse-action reasons could be lifted from the Beacon score; applicants are not told AI is involved
Potential Impact: Unfair or non-compliant adverse-action notices; inability to answer complaints or supervisor questions; loss of applicant trust
Existing Controls: Adverse-action reasons must come from the adjudicator's own assessment and may not cite the Beacon score alone; reason codes plus SHAP explanations for the Review Priority Model
Control Gap: Reason code faithfulness not validated; no source-citation standard for LLM summaries; applicant disclosure position unresolved (OI-01; OI-09)
Recommended Control: Validate reason codes during independent validation; require every LLM summary statement to link to a source document location and sample-audit citation accuracy; adverse-action standard citing adjudicator-assessed factors; Legal to conclude on applicant disclosure
KRI/KPI: Percent of LLM summary statements with a valid source citation in sample audit (98 percent proposed); percent of adverse-action notices citing adjudicator-assessed factors; complaints citing unexplained decisions
Escalation Trigger: Citation validity below 98 percent in any monthly sample: disable LLM summarization using the feature flag pending review
NIST AI RMF Mapping: MEASURE 2.8; MEASURE 2.9; GenAI Profile risk: Confabulation
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.8 (information for interested parties); Annex A.6 (documentation)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 13 (transparency to deployers); Art. 86 (explanation of individual decisions). Benchmark only
Intake Reference: Sections E; G; K; OI-01; OI-09

AI Risk: Model drift and degradation over time
Description: Applicant population; economic conditions or products change so scores lose accuracy or shift outcomes for some groups
Cause: Six-year training window; changing rates and employment conditions; product or channel changes; outcome lag delays performance evidence
Potential Impact: Accuracy and fairness degrade unnoticed; credit losses; unplanned redevelopment
Existing Controls: Enterprise model change process with re-validation
Control Gap: Drift monitoring not built; no thresholds set; fairness not monitored separately from accuracy; retraining triggers untested
Recommended Control: Monthly stability monitoring of score and top features; fairness indicators tracked on the same cadence; quarterly backtesting as outcomes mature; documented retraining triggers and re-validation
KRI/KPI: Population Stability Index on score and top features (0.10 watch and 0.25 investigate are common industry conventions); fairness ratio trend
Escalation Trigger: PSI above 0.25 on the score or any top-10 feature for two consecutive months: open model review and notify Model Risk Management
